title: Segal presheaves and coefficient localization
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. For a small monoidal infinity category $C$, put $P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Spc})$. Day convolution on $P(C)$ is left Kan extension of the external cartesian product of presheaves along the opposite of the tensor functor $C\times C\to C$. Write $C_\otimes\to\Delta$ for the cartesian fibration corresponding to $C^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$; its fibre at $[n]$ is $C^n$. Write $[n](c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ for its objects, $\Delta^n(\boldsymbol c)$ for their represented presheaves on $C_\otimes$, and $v=\Delta^0$ for the vertex representable. The labelled spine is the iterated pushout of edge representables over their common vertex representables. A Segal presheaf is $Z\in P(C_\otimes)$ for which
$$Z([n](\boldsymbol c))\longrightarrow Z([1](c_1))\times_{Z([0])}\cdots\times_{Z([0])}Z([1](c_n))$$
is an equivalence for every $n\geq2$ and every list $\boldsymbol c$. Their full subcategory is $Q_C$.

For $\phi\in P(C)$ let $J_C(\phi)$ be left Kan extension along the fibre inclusion $C^{\mathrm{op}}=(C_\otimes^{\mathrm{op}})_{[1]}\hookrightarrow C_\otimes^{\mathrm{op}}$, and let $a_\phi=\operatorname{colim}_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}\phi$. For a space $a$ and presheaf $F$, the copower $a\cdot F$ has values $a\times F(-)$. Define the free edge with two specified endpoints by the presheaf pushout
$$E_C(\phi)=J_C(\phi)\amalg_{a_\phi\cdot(v\amalg v)}(v\amalg v).$$
The two maps $v\to\Delta^1(c)$, natural in $c$, give the first leg of this pushout after the Yoneda colimit expression of $\phi$; the second leg forgets $a_\phi$. Equivalently this is the colimit of the represented edges $\Delta^1(c)$ indexed by the category of elements of $\phi$, taken in the category of presheaves under $v\amalg v$. In particular $E_C(\varnothing)=v\amalg v$.

For a small set $S$ of arrows of $P(C)$, let $P^S(C)$ be the full subcategory of $S$-local objects: $M$ is local if $\operatorname{Map}(\psi,M)\to\operatorname{Map}(\phi,M)$ is an equivalence for each $(\phi\to\psi)\in S$. Call $S$ monoidally compatible if tensoring any arrow of $S$ on either side with any presheaf becomes an equivalence after $S$-localization. Let $Q_C^S\subset Q_C$ consist of the Segal presheaves local for all arrows $E_C(\phi)\to E_C(\psi)$ induced by $S$. For $Z\in Q_C$ and $(x,y)\in Z([0])^2$, write
$$H_Z(x,y)(c)=\operatorname{fib}_{(x,y)}\bigl(Z([1](c))\longrightarrow Z([0])^2\bigr)$$
for its mapping presheaf. A Segal equivalence is a map inverted by reflection into $Q_C$; an $S$-local Segal equivalence is a map in $Q_C$ inverted by reflection into $Q_C^S$. Denote these reflectors, when they exist, by $L_C$ and $L_C^S$; denote inclusions by $i_C$ and $i_C^S$, respectively.

For small monoidal $C,D$, define $X\boxtimes Y$ by
$$(X\boxtimes Y)([n](\boldsymbol c,\boldsymbol d))=X([n](\boldsymbol c))\times Y([n](\boldsymbol d)).$$
For monoidally compatible sets $S,T$, let $S\odot T$ consist of $s\boxtimes y(d)$ and $y(c)\boxtimes t$ in $P(C\times D)$, for $s\in S,t\in T,c\in C,d\in D$, where $y$ is Yoneda and this external product is the product of presheaf values. Its domain distinguishes this notation from the operadic algebroid external product.
